cases.text: Customer: ask for one paper food card at table two.
cases.fact: The item and table both matter.
cases.next_step: Give the details clearly and check the reply.
cases.staff_note: Use an adult customer if a peer role is uncomfortable.

cases.text: Order taker: show or read the item and table back.
cases.fact: The customer can correct an error now.
cases.staff_note: Record the actual response and mode.

cases.text: Handover: receive the order and repeat its key details.
cases.fact: A clear handover reduces a message gap.
cases.next_step: Confirm the item and table before moving the empty tray.
cases.staff_note: No food is carried or served.

cases.text: Customer: ask whether the proposed item contains milk.
cases.fact: The ingredient answer is not supplied by the name.
cases.next_step: Ask the responsible adult to check current information.
cases.staff_note: Practise the referral; do not invent an ingredient list.

cases.text: Observer: one table has no clear tidy-up role.
cases.fact: The plan leaves an action unowned.
cases.next_step: Record the finding and add a proposed role.
cases.staff_note: This is a fictional prompt; actual observations stay separate.

cases.text: The visitor slot is still unconfirmed.
cases.fact: There is no external encounter to record.
cases.next_step: Use the adult customer in class and label the rehearsal.
cases.staff_note: No attendance, placement or guest feedback is invented.

Purpose and success checks
The weekly scheme line above is shared across two lessons. This lesson focuses on trying the service plan.
What does a dry rehearsal show us about the plan?
I can sequence a planned service task. I can practise a clear order handover. I can use the rehearsal to revise the plan.
VOC-W6-L2-E1: Individual service sequence and contribution, actual dry-rehearsal observation, reasoned plan revision, pending real-event checks and a recorded in-class alternative.
Before pupils arrive

Bring the Lesson 1 proposals. Print the six role/order cards. Use only paper food images, empty cups and an empty tray; no food, hot liquid, payment or equipment operation. Agree an adult or willing peer audience and an accessible mode. A visitor, placement, event date and external guests remain unconfirmed.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.
Calendar and continuity

Monday 7–Friday 11 December 2026. Two 40-minute lessons this week. No teaching day or clock slot is inferred. Any visitor, placement or external audience is unconfirmed; the in-class route is ready to use.
Staff enter the actual teaching date above. Continue the accepted prior-week evidence and support routines.

Access and practice
Supported: use the order and role prompts. Independent: rehearse the planned handover. Aspire: try one change and compare what happens.

Use a three-role dry rehearsal: customer, order taker and handover/observer. With a pair, the adult covers the third role; solo participation is possible. Run a short sequence, record one actual observation, revise a step, then retry if time allows. The written plan remains a proposal; the rehearsal does not establish food-preparation or real-service competence.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

Dry practice only. No real food, hot drinks, sharp tools, payment or live customer contact. Staff handle any later booking, permissions, risk assessment and food-safety arrangements. A rehearsal is labelled as rehearsal on all records.
Unconfirmed slot and in class alternative

Unconfirmed. No booking, invitation, placement or event date is asserted. Run the entire sequence in class with an adult as the customer. Use paper food cards and an empty tray. If a visitor is later confirmed, retain the classroom plan and record only the encounter that actually happens.
Assessment and feedback

Look for a coherent welcome/order/check/handover/tidy sequence with owners. Assess a clear read-back or accessible equivalent, accurate referral of the allergen question, and a revision grounded in what really occurred. Retain learner words, support and rehearsal context. Do not award actual food handling from paper practice.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence banked). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio
Explain a choice, listen to feedback and write or dictate a reflection. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own Communication portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.

Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Use an adult customer if a peer role is uncomfortable.

Common misunderstandings
A smooth paper rehearsal does not prove that food controls are ready. An ingredient question needs accurate current information. A proposed visitor cannot be marked as attended.

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
